## Motivation

With `--enable-metrics` and `--tokenizer-worker-num > 1`, the HTTP request
metrics are silently missing from `/metrics`:

- `sglang:http_requests_total`
- `sglang:http_responses_total`
- `sglang:http_requests_active`
- `sglang:routing_keys_active`

Per-endpoint request rates, in-flight counts and 5xx ratios therefore cannot be
monitored on a multi-tokenizer deployment, even though `/metrics` itself is
served fine.

## Modifications

The track-response middleware was registered from `_setup_and_run_http_server`,
which runs in the parent process. With `--tokenizer-worker-num > 1` the server
is started with `uvicorn.run("...:app", workers=N)`: uvicorn spawns the HTTP
workers and each one re-imports `http_server`, so the app they actually serve is
a fresh object that never received the middleware.

- Register the middleware while the module is imported (next to the existing
  `CORSMiddleware` / `RequestDecompressionMiddleware` registrations) so that
  every tokenizer worker picks it up, and drop the parent-process registration.
- Create the metrics themselves in a separate step, `init_http_request_metrics`,
  called from the lifespan once the process has published its config.
  `prometheus_client` fixes its value backend when it is first imported, and
  SGLang only sets `PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR` in `_set_envs_and_config`, which
  runs *after* `http_server` has been imported. Creating the metrics at import
  time would therefore leave them in the in-memory registry, where the
  `MultiProcessCollector` behind `/metrics` never sees them -- including in
  single-tokenizer mode.
- The middleware now runs inside each worker, so also expose that worker's
  in-flight request count as `sglang:http_worker_active_requests{worker_id}`.
  This is the number to watch when a shared listening socket concentrates
  connections on a few workers.

A unit test in `test/registered/unit/observability/test_http_request_metrics.py`
covers all three: that the middleware is on the module-level app, that importing
`http_server` does not pull `prometheus_client` in early, and that a worker
process records the counters and labels the per-worker gauge.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A - metrics only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A - no change to the inference path. With metrics enabled the per-request work
is unchanged; with metrics disabled the middleware returns after one config
lookup.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with
      pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit
      tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write
      documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
      Not applicable: `docs/docs/references/production_metrics.mdx` does not
      document the HTTP request metrics at all, so adding only the new one would
      be inconsistent.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the
      accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy)
      and [Benchmark the
      speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

+from typing import Dict, Optional, Tuple
+
+
+class RefCountedGauge:
+    def __init__(self, gauge):
+        self._gauge = gauge
+        self._refcount: Dict[str, int] = {}
+
+    def inc(self, key: str):
+        if key in self._refcount:
+            self._refcount[key] += 1
+        else:
+            self._refcount[key] = 1
+            self._gauge.inc()
+
+    def dec(self, key: str):
+        if key in self._refcount:
+            self._refcount[key] -= 1
+            if self._refcount[key] == 0:
+                del self._refcount[key]
+                self._gauge.dec()
+
+
+class _HttpRequestMetrics:
+    def __init__(self):
+        from prometheus_client import Counter, Gauge
+
+        self.requests_total = Counter(
+            name="sglang:http_requests_total",
+            documentation="Total number of HTTP requests by endpoint and method",
+            labelnames=["endpoint", "method"],
+        )
+
+        self.responses_total = Counter(
+            name="sglang:http_responses_total",
+            documentation="Total number of HTTP responses by endpoint and status code",
+            labelnames=["endpoint", "status_code", "method"],
+        )
+
+        self.requests_active = Gauge(
+            name="sglang:http_requests_active",
+            documentation="Number of currently active HTTP requests",
+            labelnames=["endpoint", "method"],
+            multiprocess_mode="livesum",
+        )
+
+        self.routing_keys_active = RefCountedGauge(
+            Gauge(
+                name="sglang:routing_keys_active",
+                documentation="Number of unique routing keys with active requests",
+                multiprocess_mode="livesum",
+            )
+        )
+
+
+_http_request_metrics: Optional[_HttpRequestMetrics] = None
+
+
+def init_http_request_metrics():
+    # Call after PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR is set: prometheus_client picks its
+    # value backend on import.
+    global _http_request_metrics
+    if _http_request_metrics is None:
+        _http_request_metrics = _HttpRequestMetrics()
+
+
+def add_http_request_metrics_middleware(app):
+    """Records nothing until init_http_request_metrics() runs in this process."""
+    # Fix: replace BaseHTTPMiddleware's call_next with a pure ASGI version
+    # that passes `receive` through, so request.is_disconnected() keeps working.
+    from sglang.srt.utils.http_middleware_patch import patch_app_http_middleware
+
+    patch_app_http_middleware(app)
+
+    @app.middleware("http")
+    async def track_http_status_code(request, call_next):
+        metrics = _http_request_metrics
+        if metrics is None:
+            return await call_next(request)
+
+        # With recording all requests, we have the risk of high cardinality if requests have arbitrary unhandled paths.
+        # But given that SGLang engines with metrics enabled are usually behind routers this looks safe.
+        path, is_handled_path = _get_fastapi_request_path(request)
+        method = request.method
+        routing_key = request.headers.get("x-smg-routing-key")
+
+        metrics.requests_total.labels(endpoint=path, method=method).inc()
+        metrics.requests_active.labels(endpoint=path, method=method).inc()
+        if routing_key:
+            metrics.routing_keys_active.inc(routing_key)
+
+        try:
+            response = await call_next(request)
+
+            metrics.responses_total.labels(
+                endpoint=path,
+                method=method,
+                status_code=str(response.status_code),
+            ).inc()
+
+            return response
+        finally:
+            metrics.requests_active.labels(endpoint=path, method=method).dec()
+            if routing_key:
+                metrics.routing_keys_active.dec(routing_key)
+
+
+# https://github.com/blueswen/fastapi-observability/blob/132a3c576f8b09e5311c68bd553215013bc75685/fastapi_app/utils.py#L98
+def _get_fastapi_request_path(request) -> Tuple[str, bool]:
+    from starlette.routing import Match
+
+    for route in request.app.routes:
+        match, child_scope = route.matches(request.scope)
+        if match == Match.FULL:
+            return getattr(route, "path", request.url.path), True
+
+    return request.url.path, False

+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=15, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+import unittest
+
+from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
+from prometheus_client import REGISTRY
+
+import sglang.srt.entrypoints.http_server as http_server
+from sglang.srt.observability import http_request_metrics
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+UNKNOWN_PATH = "/__no_such_route__"
+
+
+class TestHttpRequestMetrics(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_module_level_app_records_requests(self):
+        # Tokenizer workers re-import http_server and serve its module-level app,
+        # so the middleware must be on it, while the metrics must wait for
+        # init_http_request_metrics().
+        self.assertIsNone(http_request_metrics._http_request_metrics)
+
+        http_request_metrics.init_http_request_metrics()
+        TestClient(http_server.app).get(UNKNOWN_PATH)
+
+        self.assertEqual(
+            1.0,
+            REGISTRY.get_sample_value(
+                "sglang:http_requests_total",
+                {"endpoint": UNKNOWN_PATH, "method": "GET"},
+            ),
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
